steps.title: Check the Wi-Fi switch and airplane mode
steps.detail: Make sure the laptop's Wi-Fi switch or function key is turned on and airplane mode is off. Then confirm the laptop is connected to the correct network.

steps.title: Move closer to the router
steps.detail: Sit closer to the Wi-Fi router or access point and see whether the connection stays steady over the next hour or two.

steps.title: Forget and rejoin the Wi-Fi network
steps.detail: Open the Wi-Fi settings, choose the network, select the option to forget it, then connect again and enter the Wi-Fi password.

steps.title: Check for updates
steps.detail: Open Windows Update or your system's update settings and install any available updates, including wireless driver updates. Restart when the updates finish.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the whole laptop. This clears temporary network problems that can build up over time.

steps.detail: Click the Wi-Fi icon in the taskbar and look at the network name shown at the top. If it says guest, you are on the guest network, which usually has no internet access for work.

steps.title: Forget the guest network and rejoin your usual network

steps.detail: Look at the printer's display or lights for paper jams, an empty tray or low toner. Clear any jam or refill paper if needed.

steps.detail: Make sure the printer is switched on and its cable is firmly pushed in, or that it shows as connected to the Wi-Fi network.

steps.title: Cancel the stuck print job
steps.detail: Open the printer queue from the printer's name in your Settings or Control Panel, then cancel the job that has been printing for 20 minutes. Other jobs should then continue.

steps.title: Restart the printer
steps.detail: Turn the printer off, wait about 30 seconds, then turn it back on. Wait for it to finish starting before sending a test page.

steps.title: Send the document again
steps.detail: Print the document once more to check that the printer responds. If it still gets stuck, restart your computer and try again.

steps.title: Check the sound output device
steps.detail: Click the speaker icon in the taskbar and confirm the output is set to the laptop speakers, not a Bluetooth headset or an unplugged device. Choose the correct speakers if needed.

steps.title: Check sound settings for the app
steps.detail: Open Sound settings and look at the volume mixer to make sure the app is not muted or turned down. Adjust the app volume up if needed.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the whole laptop. Test sound again after it starts up.

steps.title: Check the toner or ink level
steps.detail: Look at the printer's display or its companion app to see whether toner or ink is low. If it is low, the printout will look faded, so replacing it may solve the problem.

steps.title: Set print quality to the highest setting
steps.detail: Open the Print dialog, select your printer, and open its preferences. Change the quality setting to High or Best, then print again.

steps.title: Print a test page from the printer
steps.detail: Use the printer's control panel to print a test or configuration page. If the test page is also faded or streaked, the problem is with the printer rather than the document.

steps.title: Run the printer's cleaning cycle
steps.detail: Open the printer's maintenance or tools menu and start the Cleaning option. Wait for it to finish, then print a test page to see if the streaks are gone.

steps.title: Restart the printer
steps.detail: Turn the printer off, wait about 30 seconds, and turn it back on. Wait until it shows Ready, then print a test page.

steps.title: Check that you are not muted
steps.detail: Look at the microphone icon in Teams and the mute button on your keyboard or headset. Unmute yourself and say a few words to check the mic light or the mic icon moves.

steps.title: Check the microphone cable
steps.detail: If you use a headset or USB microphone, unplug it and plug it back in firmly. Make sure the plug is pushed all the way in at the computer.

steps.title: Restart Teams
steps.detail: Quit Teams completely, then open it again. Join a test call to see whether people can hear you now.

steps.title: Choose the right microphone in Teams
steps.detail: Open Teams settings, go to Devices, and pick the microphone you are using under Microphone. Use the test call option to check that your voice shows on the level bar.

steps.title: Check the input device in sound settings
steps.detail: Open Windows sound settings and look under Input. Select your microphone and speak to confirm the level bar moves, and make sure its volume is not set to zero.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: Restart the whole computer, then open Teams and make a test call before your next meeting.

steps.title: Check for a privacy shutter or camera switch
steps.detail: Look at the top edge of the screen for a small sliding cover or a camera on/off key. Make sure the cover is open and the camera is switched on.

steps.title: Close other apps that might be using the camera
steps.detail: Close Teams, Zoom, Skype, or any other app or browser tab that might be using the camera. Then open your video call again.

steps.title: Restart the video call app
steps.detail: Close the video call app completely, then open it again. Check whether the camera now shows your picture.

steps.title: Check camera permissions in Settings
steps.detail: Open Settings, go to Privacy & security, then Camera. Make sure camera access is turned on for the app you use for calls.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the laptop. After it starts up, try the video call again.

steps.title: Press the brightness keys
steps.detail: Press the brightness up key, usually a sun icon on the top row of the keyboard, a few times. On some laptops you need to hold the Fn key while pressing it.

steps.title: Check the brightness slider
steps.detail: Open the Action Center or Quick Settings from the taskbar and drag the brightness slider up. You can also open Settings, go to System, then Display, and raise the brightness there.

steps.title: Turn off battery saver
steps.detail: Open Settings and go to System, then Battery. Turn off Battery saver or Energy saver, since it can dim the screen to save power.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the laptop from the Start menu. A restart often clears display problems caused by a glitch.

steps.title: Check the cable connections
steps.detail: Make sure both ends of the video cable are pushed firmly into the laptop or adapter and the monitor. Try a different port on the laptop if it has one.

steps.title: Check the monitor's input source
steps.detail: Use the monitor's buttons or menu to select the input that matches the port you plugged into, such as HDMI or USB-C. Many monitors show 'No signal' when they're set to the wrong input.

steps.title: Unplug and plug back in the cable
steps.detail: Disconnect the cable from the laptop and the monitor, wait a few seconds, then connect it again. Make sure the monitor is turned on.

steps.title: Detect the monitor in display settings
steps.detail: On Windows, press Windows key + P and choose Extend. If the monitor still isn't listed, select Detect in Settings > System > Display.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save your work, restart the laptop, and then check whether the external monitor shows a picture after it starts up.

steps.title: Try a different USB port
steps.detail: Move the USB receiver to another USB port on the computer, preferably one directly on the computer rather than a hub. Check whether the pointer moves.

steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the computer. After it starts again, test the mouse before doing anything else.

steps.detail: Plug in the laptop charger and make sure the cable is pushed in firmly at both ends. Wait a moment and then press a key again.

steps.detail: Plug the charger into a different wall outlet that you know works, such as one with a lamp or phone charger in it. If the power strip has a switch, make sure it is turned on.

steps.detail: Look at the small light on the power brick or cable, if it has one. If that light is on, the charger is getting power and the problem is likely in the laptop's port.

steps.detail: Shut the laptop down completely, leave the charger connected, and then turn it back on. Check whether the charging light comes on after it restarts.

steps.title: Save a copy and edit that copy
steps.detail: In Word, choose File > Save As and save the document to your Documents folder. Then type in the new copy, which should not be read-only.

rawSteps.title: Ask your coworker to resend the file
rawSteps.detail: Message your coworker and ask whether they saved the file as read-only or can send a fresh copy. A new copy may open for editing right away.

rawSteps.title: Check the file's Read-only setting
rawSteps.detail: Right-click the Word file, choose Properties, and uncheck Read-only if it is ticked. Then click OK and open the file again.
